findings.what: Three parallel auto-download setters exist (TGClient+Network.m:513 -setAutoDownloadSettings:networkKind:completion:, TGClient+Storage.m:571 -setAutoDownloadSettings:forNetworkType:, TGClient+Files.m:580 -setAutoDownloadSettings:forNetwork:completion:) and they disagree on the input key vocabulary; the Files copy reads `from[@"lessDataForCalls"] ?: @NO` while Network's preset dictionaries emit `useLessDataForCalls` (TGClient+Network.m:153).
findings.failure: TGClient+Files.h:213-218 documents the key as "lessDataForCalls" but tells the caller to obtain the dictionary from TGClient+Network's -autoDownloadPresetsWithCompletion:, which emits "useLessDataForCalls". Feeding a Network preset into the Files setter silently sends use_less_data_for_calls=false, and also defaults is_auto_download_enabled to @YES (line 586) where Network/Storage default to NO, so an empty dictionary turns auto-download ON instead of OFF.
findings.fix: Delete -setAutoDownloadSettings:forNetwork:completion: from TGClient+Files.m/.h (it has no callers) and route everything through TGClient+Network.m's TGNetSettingsObject/TGNetSettingsDict pair; if it must stay, change line 594 to read from[@"useLessDataForCalls"] and line 586 default to @NO.

findings.what: -setAutoDownloadSettings:forNetworkType: uses a third key vocabulary ("maxPhoto"/"maxVideo"/"maxOther") while Network uses "maxPhotoSize"/"maxVideoSize"/"maxOtherSize" (TGClient+Network.m:146-148), and it hard-codes `@"preload_stories" : @NO` (line 585) because TGStorageAutoDownloadFromPreset (line 105) never carries that field through.
findings.failure: TGSettingsViewController.m:830 reads the Storage mirror while line 837 reads `preset[@"maxPhotoSize"]` from Network presets — the two halves of one settings row speak different dialects, so any future code that hands a Network preset to the Storage setter gets max_photo_file_size = 1 MB default instead of the preset value, and every write through Storage clears the server's preload_stories flag.
findings.fix: Pick one vocabulary (Network's maxPhotoSize/maxVideoSize/maxOtherSize/preloadStories/useLessDataForCalls), rewrite TGStorageNormalizedAutoDownload (line 80), TGStorageAutoDownloadFromPreset (line 105) and the payload at lines 578-586 to use it, add a preloadStories passthrough, and update the doc block in TGClient+Storage.h:176.

findings.what: -setAutosaveScope:photos:videos:maxVideoSize: (line 370) and -setAutosaveForChat:photos:videos:maxVideoSize: (line 382) are byte-for-byte duplicates of TGClient+Storage.m:621 -setAutosavePhotos:videos:maxVideoBytes:forScope: and TGClient+Storage.m:780 -setAutosavePhotos:videos:maxVideoBytes:forChat:, down to the same setAutosaveSettings payload.
findings.failure: Both pairs are live selectors on the same TGClient object. The Storage pair clamps a non-positive size to 512 KB (Storage.m:637) while the AppSettings pair passes maxVideoSize straight through, so calling the AppSettings variant with 0 sends max_video_file_size=0 and silently disables video autosave, whereas the Storage variant with the same argument enables it at 512 KB. Only the Storage pair has callers; the AppSettings pair is dead.
findings.fix: Delete -setAutosaveScope:photos:videos:maxVideoSize: and -setAutosaveForChat:photos:videos:maxVideoSize: plus TGASAutosaveScopeObject (AppSettings.m:139) from TGClient+AppSettings.m/.h; keep the Storage pair as the single autosave writer.

findings.what: The whole TGClient (Calls) category is unreachable: of the 14 methods in TGClient+Calls.h only -rateCallId:rating:comment:problems:completion: has a caller anywhere in src/. -callLogWithOffset:, -frequentlyCalledContactsWithCompletion:, -groupCallServiceTextForContent:, -isGroupCallLink:, -clearCallLogRevoke:, -declineGroupCallInvitationInChat:, -callNetworkUsageWithCompletion:, -resetNetworkUsageWithCompletion:, -setSessionId:canAcceptCalls:, -sendDebugInformationForCallId:, -sendLogForCallId:, -rateCallInChat:, -removeFrequentlyCalledChat: have none.
findings.failure: 390 lines of code, its string tables and its Objective-C metadata are linked into the binary and paged in at launch on a 512 MB device that has 40-60 MB of headroom, and no screen can ever reach any of it. The same is true of TGClient+Translation.m (10 of 13 public methods uncalled — the entire language-pack and speech-recognition surface, lines 214-413) and of the wallpaper/theme half of TGClient+AppSettings.m (12 of 17 public methods uncalled, lines 232-433).
findings.fix: Either delete the uncalled methods from TGClient+Calls.m/.h, TGClient+Translation.m/.h (languagePacks*, languagePackInfo:, applyLanguagePack:, synchronizeLanguagePack:, languagePackStrings:, deleteLanguagePack:, recognizeSpeechForMessage:, speechTranscriptForMessage:, rateSpeechRecognitionForMessage:, translateMessages:) and TGClient+AppSettings.m/.h (setDefaultBackground*, searchBackgroundNamed:, shareUrlForBackgroundNamed:, removeInstalledBackgroundId:, resetInstalledBackgrounds, setChatThemeEmoji:, chatThemeEmojiForChat:, applicationConfigValueForKey:), or wire the screens that were supposed to use them. Do not leave them half-alive.

findings.what: -storageUsageForChat: answers a per-chat question by fetching the global top-N list: `[self storageUsageByChatWithLimit:256 completion:...]` and then linear-scanning it for a matching chatId.
findings.failure: getStorageStatistics with chat_limit:256 groups every chat outside the 256 largest into a single entry with chat_id == 0 (td_api.tl:9685). For a user with more than 256 cached chats, asking for the cache size of a small chat returns (0, 0) — the screen shows "0 bytes" and the Clear button looks like a no-op even though files exist. It also walks the entire file cache on an A5 for one number.
findings.fix: Do not reuse the aggregate call. Either accept the imprecision explicitly by documenting the 256-chat ceiling in TGClient+Storage.h, or issue getStorageStatistics with a large chat_limit only once and cache the by_chat map, keyed by chat_id, instead of re-walking the cache per chat.

findings.what: -writeScope:settings: rebuilds the full scopeNotificationSettings object on every write and hard-codes the story fields: `@"use_default_mute_stories" : @YES, @"mute_stories" : @NO, @"story_sound_id" : @(0), @"show_story_poster" : @NO`, while -notificationSettingsForScope: (line 66) never reads them back. `use_default_mute_stories` is not even a field of scopeNotificationSettings (td_api.tl:3348 — it belongs to chatNotificationSettings).
findings.failure: Toggling any unrelated switch on the Notifications page (TGSettingsViewController.m:1873 -> -updateScope:values:completion:) resets the account's story notification settings on the server: mute_stories and show_story_poster go to false and story_sound_id to 0, clobbering whatever the user set from a modern client.
findings.fix: Add mute_stories / story_sound_id / show_story_poster to TGNotifScopeSettingsFrom (line 53) as "muteStories"/"storySoundId"/"showStoryPoster", read them back in -writeScope: from the merged dictionary instead of constants, and drop the bogus use_default_mute_stories key.

findings.what: Four of the seven error predicates in this layer send isEqualToString: to an unchecked value: `[((NSDictionary *)result)[@"@type"] isEqualToString:@"error"]` (Calls.m:6, AppSettings.m:6, Storage.m:55, Notifications.m:17). TGClient+Network.m:29-32 and TGClient+Translation.m:7-9 do type-check first, so the codebase already knows better.
findings.failure: Any reply whose "@type" is not a string — a malformed frame, or a future TDLib object where the code walks a nested dictionary through the same predicate, e.g. Calls.m:270 `[entry[@"@type"] isEqualToString:@"networkStatisticsEntryCall"]` on an entry whose @type came back as a number — raises -[__NSCFNumber isEqualToString:]: unrecognized selector and kills the app instead of being treated as an error result.
findings.fix: Replace the bodies of TGCallsIsError, TGASIsError, TGStorageFailed and TGNotifIsError with the guarded form used in TGClient+Network.m:26-33: fetch @type, `if (![type isKindOfClass:[NSString class]]) return YES;`, then compare. Same guard for the bare nested comparisons at Calls.m:136, Calls.m:270 and Storage.m:520.

findings.what: Network-type name mapping is written twice with different accepted inputs: TGStorageNetworkTypeName (Storage.m:20) accepts "cellular" and "roaming", TGNetNetworkTypeName (Network.m:65) accepts "mobileroaming" but not "cellular"/"roaming" alone. Likewise TGNetString/TGNetNumber/TGNetArray/TGNetDict, TGCallsString/TGCallsNumber/TGCallsArray/TGCallsDict, TGStorageDictionary/TGStorageArray, TGTrString/TGTrNumber/TGTrArray/TGTrDict and TGASDict are five identical copies of the same four coercion helpers.
findings.failure: TGClient+Storage.h:200 documents the network names as "wifi"/"mobile"/"roaming"/"other" and Storage.m:700 defaults to exactly that list; passing "roaming" to the Network category's -setAutoDownloadSettings:networkKind: (Network.m:513) instead maps to networkTypeOther, so a roaming preset is written to the wrong TDLib network bucket and never takes effect while roaming.
findings.fix: Keep one mapping function (the Storage one, which accepts the documented vocabulary plus aliases), expose it from TGClient+Private.h, and delete TGNetNetworkTypeName; do the same for the four coercion helpers so all seven files share one set.
